collision mesh or use hardcoded vertices\n\ndef generic_to_pybullet(\n    generic_obj: GenericObject,\n    height: float = DEFAULT_HEIGHT,\n    position: Tuple[float, float, float] = (0, 0, 0),\n kinetic_friction, we set object to 1.0 and ground to kinetic_friction\n        object_friction = 1.0  # Ground friction dominates\n    else:\n        # For robot contact scenarios: use polygon.convex_hull, physics_props, height, position, orientation, color\n        )\n\n\ndef _create_convex_body(\n    polygon: Polygon,\n    physics_props: Dict,\n    height: float,\n    position: Parameters\n    ----------\n    polygon : Polygon\n        Shapely Polygon (must be convex).\n    physics_props : dict\n        Physics properties including 'mass', 'inertia_3d', 'object_friction'.\n color.\n    \n    Returns\n    -------\n    int\n        PyBullet body UID.\n    \"\"\"\n    mass = physics_props['mass']\n    inertia_3d = physics_props['inertia_3d']  # (Ixx, Iyy, Izz)\n vertices_3d, indices = _create_polygon_mesh(coords, height)\n        collision_id = pyb.createCollisionShape(\n            shapeType=pyb.GEOM_MESH,\n            vertices=vertices_3d.tolist(),\n   rollingFriction=0.01,\n        linearDamping=0.0,\n        angularDamping=0.0\n    )\n    \n    return uid\n\n\ndef _create_triangle_mesh(coords_2d, height):\n    \"\"\"Create a 3D triangle mesh vertices_3d = []\n    indices = []\n    \n    # Bottom face vertices (z = 0)\n    for x, y in coords_2d:\n        vertices_3d.append([x, y, 0.0])\n    \n    # Top face vertices (z = height)\n    for 2-0, triangle 2\n    \n    return np.array(vertices_3d, dtype=np.float64), np.array(indices, dtype=np.int32)\n\n\ndef _create_polygon_mesh(coords_2d, height):\n    \"\"\"Create a 3D polygon mesh from 2D coordinates by extrusion.\n    \n    Parameters\n    ----------\n    coords_2d : list\n        List of (x, y) coordinates\n    height : float\n        Extrusion height\n    \n    Returns\n vertices_3d = []\n    indices = []\n    \n    # Bottom face vertices (z = 0)\n    for x, y in coords_2d:\n        vertices_3d.append([x, y, 0.0])\n    \n    # Top face vertices (z = height)\n    for \"\"\"Create a compound PyBullet body from multiple convex polygons.\n    \n    Parameters\n    ----------\n    parts : list of Polygon\n        List of convex polygons forming the compound shape.\n Tuple[float, float, float]:\n    \"\"\"Calculate 3D inertia tensor diagonal from 2D moment of inertia.\n    \n    For a 2D shape extruded to height h, the 3D inertia tensor is:\n    - Ixx: rotation around x-axis (involves height and y-extent)\n    - Iyy: rotation around y-axis (involves height and x-extent)\n    - Izz: rotation around z-axis (the original 2D moment of inertia)\n    \n    Parameters\n    ----------\n    moment_of_inertia_2d : float\n        The 2D moment of inertia (Iz) from GenericObject.\n    mass : float\n        Object mass.\n    height : float\n        Extrusion height of the object.\n    \n    Returns\n    -------\n    tuple\n        (Ixx, Iyy, Izz) inertia tensor diagonal.\n    \"\"\"\n    # For a 2D shape extruded to height h:\n    # Izz = I_2d (the planar moment of inertia)\n    # Ixx ≈ Iyy ≈ I_2d/2 + m*h²/12 (parallel axis theorem for height)\n    Izz = moment_of_inertia_2d\n    \n    # Approximation for Ixx, Iyy (assuming roughly symmetric shape)\n    height_contribution = mass * height * height / 12.0\n    Ixx = Izz / 2.0 + height_contribution\n    Iyy = Izz / 2.0 + height_contribution\n    \n    return (Ixx, Iyy, Izz)\n\n\n# ============================================================================\n# CONVEX DECOMPOSITION UTILITIES\n# ============================================================================\n\ndef is_convex(polygon: Polygon) -&gt; bool:\n    \"\"\"Check if a polygon is convex.\n    \n    Parameters\n    ----------\n    polygon : Polygon\n        Shapely Polygon to check.\n    \n    Returns\n    -------\n    bool\n        True if convex, False otherwise.\n    \"\"\"\n    coords = list(polygon.exterior.coords)[:-1]  # Remove duplicate closing point\n    n = len(coords)\n    \n    if n &lt; 3:\n        return False\n    \n    sign = None\n    for i in range(n):\n        p1 = coords[i]\n        p2 = coords[(i + 1) % n]\n        p3 = coords[(i + 2) % n]\n        \n        # Cross product of edges\n        cross = (p2[0] - p1[0]) * (p3[1] - p2[1]) - (p2[1] - p1[1]) * (p3[0] - p2[0])\n        \n        if sign is None:\n            sign = cross &gt; 0\n        elif (cross &gt; 0) != sign and abs(cross) &gt; 1e-10:\n            return False\n    \n    return True\n\n\ndef decompose_to_convex_parts(polygon: Polygon) -&gt; List[Polygon]:\n    \"\"\"Decompose a non-convex polygon into convex parts.\n    \n    Supports:\n    - Triangles (already convex, returned as-is)\n    - Rectangles (already convex, returned as-is)\n    - L-shapes (decomposed into 2 rectangles)\n    - T-shapes (decomposed into 2 rectangles)\n    \n    For other shapes, falls back to convex hull approximation.\n    \n    ⚠️  KNOWN ISSUES:\n        - L-shape: Physics and t-param compatibility are quite okay\n        - T-shape: Has problems with t-param and cannot provide correct transformation\n                   (physics behavior not tested yet)\n        - Triangle: Physics is wrong (objects don't rotate when pushed at corners).\n                   This is weird since triangles should be simpler than rectilinear shapes.\n                   Double-check triangle creation vs rectilinear - the more complex shapes\n                   (L/T) work but the simple triangle doesn't, which is funny.\n    \n    Parameters\n    ----------\n    polygon : Polygon\n        Shapely Polygon to decompose.\n    \n    Returns\n    -------\n    list of Polygon\n        List of convex polygons that approximate the original.\n    \"\"\"\n    if is_convex(polygon):\n        return [polygon]\n    \n    # For L-shape and T-shape, use manual decomposition\n    coords = list(polygon.exterior.coords)[:-1]\n    n = len(coords)\n    \n    # Triangles are already convex (3 vertices)\n    if n == 3:\n        return [polygon]\n    \n    # Try simple rectangle decomposition for L/T shapes (6-8 vertices)\n    if 6 &lt;= n &lt;= 12:\n        return _decompose_rectilinear(polygon)\n    \n    # Fallback: use convex hull (loses concave detail)\n    return [polygon.convex_hull]\n\n\ndef _decompose_rectilinear(polygon: Polygon) -&gt; List[Polygon]:\n    \"\"\"Decompose rectilinear polygon (L, T shapes) into rectangles.\n    \n    Simple, direct approach for L and T shapes only.\n    Creates perfect tiling with no gaps.\n    \n    ⚠️  KNOWN ISSUES:\n        - L-shape: Physics and t-param compatibility are quite okay\n        - T-shape: Has problems with t-param and cannot provide correct transformation\n                   (physics behavior not tested yet)\n    \"\"\"\n    coords = list(polygon.exterior.coords)[:-1]\n    n = len(coords)\n    \n    # Get unique x and y coordinates (sorted)\n    xs = sorted(set(c[0] for c in coords))\n    ys = sorted(set(c[1] for c in coords))\n    minx, miny, maxx, maxy = polygon.bounds\n    \n    # For L-shape (6 vertices): always has 3 unique x and 3 unique y values\n    # NOTE: L-shape has quite okay physics and t-param compatibility\n    if n == 6:\n        # L-shape decomposition: two rectangles that share a corner\n        # The corner is always at one of the middle coordinates\n        \n        # Try Option 1: Horizontal base (bottom) + Vertical arm (left)\n        # Base: xs[0] to xs[2], ys[0] to ys[1]\n        # Arm: xs[0] to xs[1], ys[1] to ys[2]\n        rect1 = Polygon([\n            (xs[0], ys[0]), (xs[2], ys[0]), (xs[2], ys[1]), (xs[0], ys[1])\n        ])\n        rect2 = Polygon([\n            (xs[0], ys[1]), (xs[1], ys[1]), (xs[1], ys[2]), (xs[0], ys[2])\n        ])\n        \n        # Check if this decomposition works (rectangles are contained in polygon)\n        if rect1.within(polygon.buffer(1e-6)) and rect2.within(polygon.buffer(1e-6)):\n            # Verify they cover the polygon\n            union_area = rect1.union(rect2).area\n            if abs(union_area - polygon.area) &lt; 1e-4:\n                return [rect1, rect2]\n        \n        # Try Option 2: Vertical base (left) + Horizontal arm (bottom)\n        # Base: xs[0] to xs[1], ys[0] to ys[2]\n        # Arm: xs[1] to xs[2], ys[0] to ys[1]\n        rect1 = Polygon([\n            (xs[0], ys[0]), (xs[1], ys[0]), (xs[1], ys[2]), (xs[0], ys[2])\n        ])\n        rect2 = Polygon([\n            (xs[1], ys[0]), (xs[2], ys[0]), (xs[2], ys[1]), (xs[1], ys[1])\n        ])\n        \n        if rect1.within(polygon.buffer(1e-6)) and rect2.within(polygon.buffer(1e-6)):\n            union_area = rect1.union(rect2).area\n            if abs(union_area - polygon.area) &lt; 1e-4:\n                return [rect1, rect2]\n        \n        # Try Option 3: Horizontal base (top) + Vertical arm (right)\n        # Base: xs[0] to xs[2], ys[1] to ys[2]\n        # Arm: xs[1] to xs[2], ys[0] to ys[1]\n        rect1 = Polygon([\n            (xs[0], ys[1]), (xs[2], ys[1]), (xs[2], ys[2]), (xs[0], ys[2])\n        ])\n        rect2 = Polygon([\n            (xs[1], ys[0]), (xs[2], ys[0]), (xs[2], ys[1]), (xs[1], ys[1])\n        ])\n        \n        if rect1.within(polygon.buffer(1e-6)) and rect2.within(polygon.buffer(1e-6)):\n            union_area = rect1.union(rect2).area\n            if abs(union_area - polygon.area) &lt; 1e-4:\n                return [rect1, rect2]\n        \n        # Try Option 4: Vertical base (right) + Horizontal arm (top)\n        # Base: xs[1] to xs[2], ys[0] to ys[2]\n        # Arm: xs[0] to xs[1], ys[1] to ys[2]\n        rect1 = Polygon([\n            (xs[1], ys[0]), (xs[2], ys[0]), (xs[2], ys[2]), (xs[1], ys[2])\n        ])\n        rect2 = Polygon([\n            (xs[0], ys[1]), (xs[1], ys[1]), (xs[1], ys[2]), (xs[0], ys[2])\n        ])\n        \n        if rect1.within(polygon.buffer(1e-6)) and rect2.within(polygon.buffer(1e-6)):\n            union_area = rect1.union(rect2).area\n            if abs(union_area - polygon.area) &lt;     "content": "#!/usr/bin/env python3\n\"\"\"\nSimple test to verify OBJ-to-GenericObject conversion.\n\nThis script:\n1. Loads an object from OBJ file and converts it to GenericObject\n2. Periodically traverses through t_param (over 2 seconds)\n3. Draws markers to visualize:\n   - Contact point position (what GenericObject thinks it is)\n   - Normal outward vector\n   - Tangent vector\n4. This helps verify if the conversion from OBJ to GenericObject is correct\n\"\"\"\n\nimport sys\nimport time\nfrom pathlib import Path\nfrom typing import Optional\n\nimport numpy as np\nimport pybullet as pyb\nimport pybullet_data\nimport rospkg\n\n# Use non-interactive backend for headless mode\nimport matplotlib\nmatplotlib.use('Agg')\nimport matplotlib.pyplot as plt\n\n# ROS package path setup\nrospack = rospkg.RosPack()\npkg_path = rospack.get_path(\"contact_maintain\")\nsys.path.insert(0, str(Path(pkg_path) / \"src\"))\nsys.path.insert(0, str(Path(pkg_path) / \"src\" / \"legacy\"))\n\nfrom object_utils import ContactPointParameterization\nfrom contact_maintain.object_bridge import obj_to_generic\n\n# Constants\nTIMESTEP = 1.0 / 240.0\nDEFAULT_OBJECT_FRICTION = 0.8\nT_PARAM_INCREMENT_INTERVAL = 2.0  # seconds between t_param increments\nT_PARAM_INCREMENT = 0.1  # increment amount\n\n\ndef setup_pybullet(gui: bool = True):\n    \"\"\"Initialize PyBullet.\"\"\"\n    if gui:\n        client_id = pyb.connect(pyb.GUI, options=\"--width=1280 --height=720\")\n    else:\n        client_id = pyb.connect(pyb.DIRECT)\n    \n    pyb.setGravity(0, 0, -9.81)\n    pyb.setTimeStep(TIMESTEP)\n    pyb.setRealTimeSimulation(0)\n    \n    # Set search paths BEFORE loading any URDF files (PyBullet requirement)\n    pyb.setAdditionalSearchPath(pybullet_data.getDataPath())\n    ground = pyb.loadURDF(\"plane.urdf\", [0, 0, 0])\n\n    # Add URDF directory to search path for custom OBJ files\n    urdf_dir = Path(pkg_path) / \"urdf\"\n    if urdf_dir.exists():\n        pyb.setAdditionalSearchPath(str(urdf_dir))\n    \n    pyb.changeDynamics(ground, -1, lateralFriction=DEFAULT_OBJECT_FRICTION)\n    \n    if gui:\n        pyb.resetDebugVisualizerCamera(\n            cameraDistance=3.0,\n            cameraYaw=45,\n            cameraPitch=-45,\n            cameraTargetPosition=[0, 0, 0]\n        )\n        pyb.configureDebugVisualizer(pyb.COV_ENABLE_GUI, 0)\n    \n    return ground\n\n\ndef create_marker(position: np.ndarray, color: tuple = (1.0, 0.0, 0.0, 1.0), radius: float = 0.03):\n    \"\"\"Create a visual marker at position.\"\"\"\n    marker_uid = pyb.createVisualShape(\n        shapeType=pyb.GEOM_SPHERE,\n        radius=radius,\n        rgbaColor=color\n    )\n    body_uid = pyb.createMultiBody(\n        baseMass=0,\n        baseVisualShapeIndex=marker_uid,\n        basePosition=[position[0], position[1], 0.1],\n        baseOrientation=[0, 0, 0, 1]\n    )\n    return body_uid\n\n\ndef create_arrow_marker(start_pos: np.ndarray, direction: np.ndarray, color: tuple = (0.0, 1.0, 0.0, 1.0), scale: float = 0.2):\n    \"\"\"Create an arrow marker to visualize a vector direction.\"\"\"\n    # Normalize direction and scale\n    direction_norm = direction / (np.linalg.norm(direction) + 1e-10)\n    end_pos = start_pos + direction_norm * scale\n    \n    # Create a cylinder for the arrow shaft\n    arrow_length = np.linalg.norm(end_pos - start_pos)\n    mid_pos = (start_pos + end_pos) / 2\n    \n    # Calculate rotation to align with direction\n    angle = np.arctan2(direction_norm[1], direction_norm[0])\n    orn = pyb.getQuaternionFromEuler([0, 0, angle])\n    \n    arrow_uid = pyb.createVisualShape(\n        shapeType=pyb.GEOM_CYLINDER,\n        radius=0.01,\n        length=arrow_length,\n        rgbaColor=color\n    )\n    body_uid = pyb.createMultiBody(\n        baseMass=0,\n        baseVisualShapeIndex=arrow_uid,\n        basePosition=[mid_pos[0], mid_pos[1], 0.1],\n        baseOrientation=orn\n    )\n    return body_uid\n\n\ndef main():\n    import argparse\n    \n    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=\"Test OBJ+DXF-to-GenericObject conversion\")\n    parser.add_argument(\n        \"--obj-shape\",\n        type=str,\n        default=\"right_triangle\",\n        help=\"Shape name (right_triangle, bolt, pi, root; default: right_triangle)\",\n    )\n    parser.add_argument(\"--obj-file\", type=str, default=None,\n                       help=\"OBJ file path (relative to urdf directory). If None, uses '{obj-shape}.obj'\")\n    parser.add_argument(\"--duration\", type=float, default=5.0,\n                       help=\"Total test duration (default: 5.0 s)\")\n    parser.add_argument(\"--no-gui\", action=\"store_true\",\n                       help=\"Run headless\")\n    parser.add_argument(\"--save-dir\", type=str, default=None,\n                       help=\"Directory to save visualization plots\")\n    args = parser.parse_args()\n    \n    print(\"=\"*60)\n    print(\"  OBJ-to-GenericObject Conversion Test\")\n    print(\"=\"*60)\n    print(f\"  OBJ shape: {args.obj_shape}\")\n    print(f\"  t_param increment: {T_PARAM_INCREMENT:.1f} every {T_PARAM_INCREMENT_INTERVAL:.1f} s\")\n    print(f\"  Total duration: {args.duration:.1f} s\")\n    print(\"=\"*60)\n    \n    # Setup PyBullet\n    print(\"\\nInitializing PyBullet...\")\n    setup_pybullet(gui=not args.no_gui)\n    \n    # Load OBJ file and create GenericObject\n    if args.obj_file is None:\n        obj_file = f\"{args.obj_shape}.obj\"\n    else:\n        obj_file = args.obj_file\n    \n    print(f\"\\nLoading OBJ file: {obj_file}...\")\n    try:\n        generic_object, object_uid = obj_to_generic(\n            obj_path=obj_file,\n            shape_name=args.obj_shape,\n            position=(0.0, 0.0, 0.5),\n            orientation=0.0,\n            mass=2.0,\n            lateral_friction=DEFAULT_OBJECT_FRICTION\n        )\n        print(f\"✓ Loaded OBJ object: {args.obj_shape}\")\n        print(f\"  Mass: {generic_object.mass:.3f} kg\")\n        print(f\"  Moment of inertia: {generic_object.moment_of_inertia:.6f} kg·m²\")\n        print(f\"  Lateral friction: {generic_object.lateral_friction:.3f}\")\n    except Exception as e:\n        print(f\"✗ Failed to load OBJ: {e}\")\n        import traceback\n        traceback.print_exc()\n        return\n    \n    # Create contact point parameterization\n    print(f\"\\nCreating contact point parameterization...\")\n    parameterization = ContactPointParameterization(generic_object)\n    boundary_length = generic_object.boundary_length\n    print(f\"  Boundary length: {boundary_length:.3f} m\")\n    \n    # Visualize parameterization using matplotlib\n    print(f\"\\nGenerating parameterization visualization...\")\n    try:\n        ax = parameterization.visualize_parameterization(n_test_points=30)\n        \n        # Save plot if save-dir is provided\n        if args.save_dir:\n            save_path = Path(args.save_dir)\n            save_path.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)\n            plot_file = save_path / f\"{args.obj_shape}_parameterization.png\"\n            plt.savefig(plot_file, dpi=150, bbox_inches='tight')\n            print(f\"  ✓ Saved parameterization plot to: {plot_file}\")\n        else:\n            # Save to current directory as fallback\n            plot_file = Path(f\"{args.obj_shape}_parameterization.png\")\n            plt.savefig(plot_file, dpi=150, bbox_inches='tight')\n            print(f\"  ✓ Saved parameterization plot to: {plot_file}\")\n        \n        plt.close()\n    except Exception as e:\n        print(f\"  ⚠ Failed to generate visualization: {e}\")\n        import traceback\n        traceback.print_exc()\n    \n    # Delay 1 second to let physics stabilize\n    print(f\"\\nWaiting 1 second for physics to stabilize...\")\n    for _ in range(int(1.0 / TIMESTEP)):\n        pyb.stepSimulation()\n        if not args.no_gui:\n            time.sleep(TIMESTEP)\n    print(f\"  ✓ Physics stabilized\")\n    \n    # Traverse through t_param and visualize\n    print(f\"\\n{'='*60}\")\n    print(f\"  Traversing t_param: increment by {T_PARAM_INCREMENT:.1f} every {T_PARAM_INCREMENT_INTERVAL:.1f} seconds...\")\n    print(f\"{'='*60}\")\n    \n    n_steps = int(args.duration / TIMESTEP)\n    step_count = 0\n    t = 0.0\n    current_t_param = 0.0\n    last_increment_time = 0.0\n    \n    # Markers (will be updated each step)\n    contact_marker = None\n    normal_outward_marker = None\n    normal_inward_marker = None\n    tangent_marker = None\n    \n    for step in range(n_steps):\n        # Increment t_param every T_PARAM_INCREMENT_INTERVAL seconds\n        t_param_changed = False\n        if t - last_increment_time &gt;= T_PARAM_INCREMENT_INTERVAL:\n            current_t_param = (current_t_param + T_PARAM_INCREMENT) % 1.0\n            last_increment_time = t\n            t_param_changed = True\n        \n        # Only update markers when t_param changes\n        if t_param_changed:\n            # Get object's current position and orientation in world frame\n            obj_pos, obj_orn = pyb.getBasePositionAndOrientation(object_uid)\n            euler = pyb.getEulerFromQuaternion(obj_orn)\n            object_orientation = euler[2]  # Z-axis rotation\n            \n            # Get contact point info at current t_param (in body frame)\n            contact_info = parameterization.get_contact_info(current_t_param)\n            contact_point_body = contact_info['point']\n            normal_outward_body = contact_info['normal_outward']\n            normal_inward_body = -normal_outward_body\n            tangent_body = contact_info['tangent']\n            \n            # Transform to world frame\n            cos_t = np.cos(object_orientation)\n            sin_t = np.sin(object_orientation)\n            R = np.array([[cos_t, -sin_t], [sin_t, cos_t]])\n            \n            # Transform contact point to world frame\n            contact_point_world = R @ contact_point_body + np.array([obj_pos[0], obj_pos[1]])\n            \n            # Transform vectors to world frame\n            normal_outward_world = R @ normal_outward_body\n            normal_inward_world = R @ normal_inward_body\n            tangent_world = R @ tangent_body\n            \n            # Remove old markers\n            if contact_marker is not None:\n                pyb.removeBody(contact_marker)\n            if normal_outward_marker is not None:\n                pyb.removeBody(normal_outward_marker)\n            if normal_inward_marker is not None:\n                pyb.removeBody(normal_inward_marker)\n            if tangent_marker is not None:\n                pyb.removeBody(tangent_marker)\n            \n            # Create new markers in world frame\n            # Red sphere: contact point position\n            contact_marker = create_marker(\n                contact_point_world, \n                color=(1.0, 0.0, 0.0, 1.0), \n                radius=0.04\n            )\n            \n            # Green arrow: normal outward vector\n            normal_outward_marker = create_arrow_marker(\n                contact_point_world,\n                normal_outward_world,\n                color=(0.0, 1.0, 0.0, 1.0),\n                scale=0.15\n            )\n            \n            # Yellow arrow: normal inward vector (for comparison)\n            normal_inward_marker = create_arrow_marker(\n                contact_point_world,\n                normal_inward_world,\n                color=(1.0, 1.0, 0.0, 1.0),\n                scale=0.15\n            )\n            \n            # Blue arrow: tangent vector\n            tangent_marker = create_arrow_marker(\n                contact_point_world,\n                tangent_world,\n                color=(0.0, 0.0, 1.0, 1.0),\n                scale=0.15\n            )\n            \n            # Print status when t_param changes\n            print(f\"  [t={t:.2f}s] t_param={current_t_param:.3f}, \"\n                  f\"contact_point_world=({contact_point_world[0]:.3f}, {contact_point_world[1]:.3f})\")\n        \n        pyb.stepSimulation()\n        t += TIMESTEP\n        step_count += 1\n        \n        if not args.no_gui:\n            time.sleep(TIMESTEP * 0.5)\n    \n    print(f\"\\n{'='*60}\")\n    print(\"  VISUALIZATION COMPLETE\")\n    print(f\"{'='*60}\")\n    print(f\"  Red sphere: Contact point position (GenericObject's understanding)\")\n    print(f\"  Green arrow: Normal outward vector (from GenericObject)\")\n    print(f\"  Yellow arrow: Normal inward vector (for comparison)\")\n    print(f\"  Blue arrow: Tangent vector\")\n    print(f\"  Compare markers with actual 3D object to verify conversion correctness\")\n    print(f\"{'='*60}\")\n    \n    if not args.no_gui:\n        print(\"\\nMarkers will remain visible. Press Enter to exit...\")\n        input()\n    \n    pyb.disconnect()\n    print(\"\\nDone!\")\n\n\nif __name__ == \"__main__\":\n    main()\n",
    "languageId": "python"
  }
}

### What I’ve changed

- **New DXF → Generic pipeline**  
  - Added `dxf_to_generic` to `object_utils.py` to build a `GenericObject` directly from a DXF LWPOLYLINE:
    - Reads the DXF with `ezdxf`, finds the first `LWPOLYLINE`, extracts \((x, y)\) vertices (dropping the duplicate closing point if present).
    - Builds a Shapely `Polygon`, checks validity/area, estimates mass via `estimate_realistic_mass` (unless a mass is passed in), and returns a `GenericObject` with given `name`, `lateral_friction`, and `heading`.

- **`obj_to_generic` now uses DXF geometry (no JSON)**  
  - In `object_bridge.py`, `obj_to_generic` now:
    - Still loads the OBJ into PyBullet and extracts mass, friction, and 3D inertia as before.
    - Uses `dxf_to_generic` with `dxf_path = <pkg_path>/urdf/<shape_name>.dxf` to create the 2D `GenericObject` geometry.
    - Sets `generic_obj.mass` from PyBullet’s mass (if > 0), `lateral_friction` from PyBullet, `heading` from the requested orientation, and then **overrides** `generic_obj.moment_of_inertia` with PyBullet’s \(I_{zz}\).
  - Removed the old `load_shape_data` helper and all references to `shape_data.json`.
  - Deleted `/home/docker_user/catkin_ws/src/contact_maintain/urdf/shape_data.json` as requested.

- **DXF-based testing in `test_obj_to_generic.py`**  
  - Kept the call to `obj_to_generic` but it now implicitly uses DXF geometry via the updated pipeline above.
  - Updated the CLI help to reflect the new shapes:
    - `--obj-shape` now documented as: `right_triangle, bolt, pi, root` (default `right_triangle`).
  - You can now run the same t-param traversal + marker test on all four shapes, e.g.:
    - `python3 test_obj_to_generic.py --obj-shape right_triangle`
    - `python3 test_obj_to_generic.py --obj-shape bolt`
    - `python3 test_obj_to_generic.py --obj-shape pi`
    - `python3 test_obj_to_generic.py --obj-shape root`

So: geometry now always comes from the `.dxf` (via `dxf_to_generic`), PyBullet still uses the `.obj` meshes, and `test_obj_to_generic.py` can exercise all four shapes through the same interface.

Fixed the type annotation compatibility issue. The problem was using Python 3.10+ union syntax (`str | Path`, `str | None`, `float | None`). I've replaced them with `Union[str, Path]` and `Optional[str]`/`Optional[float]` from the `typing` module, which are compatible with older Python versions.

The changes:
1. Added `from typing import Union, Optional` import
2. Changed `dxf_path: str | Path` → `dxf_path: Union[str, Path]`
3. Changed `name: str | None` → `name: Optional[str]`
4. Changed `mass: float | None` → `mass: Optional[float]`
5. Removed the variable type annotation that used `list[tuple[...]]` syntax

The code should now work with Python versions that don't support the `|` union operator (Python < 3.10).

seconds between t_param increments\nT_PARAM_INCREMENT = 0.1  # increment amount\n\n\ndef setup_pybullet(gui: bool = True):\n    \"\"\"Initialize PyBullet.\"\"\"\n    if gui:\n        client_id = pyb.connect(pyb.GUI, options=\"--width=1280 --height=720\")\n    else:\n        client_id = pyb.connect(pyb.DIRECT)\n    \n    pyb.setGravity(0, 0, -9.81)\n    pyb.setTimeStep(TIMESTEP)\n    pyb.setRealTimeSimulation(0)\n    \n    # Normalize direction and scale\n    direction_norm = direction / (np.linalg.norm(direction) + 1e-10)\n    end_pos = start_pos + direction_norm * scale\n    \n    # Create a cylinder for the arrow shaft\n    arrow_length = np.linalg.norm(end_pos - start_pos)\n    mid_pos = (start_pos + end_pos) / 2\n    \n    # Setup PyBullet\n    print(\"\\nInitializing PyBullet...\")\n    setup_pybullet(gui=not args.no_gui)\n    \n    # Load OBJ file and create GenericObject\n    if args.obj_file is None:\n        obj_file = f\"{args.obj_shape}.obj\"\n    else:\n        obj_file = args.obj_file\n    \n    print(f\"\\nLoading OBJ file: {obj_file}...\")\n    try:\n        generic_object, object_uid = obj_to_generic(\n            obj_path=obj_file,\n            shape_name=args.obj_shape,\n            position=(0.0, 0.0, 0.5),\n            orientation=0.0,\n            mass=2.0,\n            lateral_friction=DEFAULT_OBJECT_FRICTION\n        )\n        print(f\"✓ Loaded OBJ object: {args.obj_shape}\")\n        print(f\"  Mass: {generic_object.mass:.3f} kg\")\n        print(f\"  Moment of inertia: {generic_object.moment_of_inertia:.6f} kg·m²\")\n        print(f\"  Lateral friction: {generic_object.lateral_friction:.3f}\")\n    except Exception as e:\n        print(f\"✗ Failed to load OBJ: {e}\")\n        import traceback\n        traceback.print_exc()\n        return\n    \n    # Create contact point parameterization\n    print(f\"\\nCreating contact point parameterization...\")\n    parameterization = ContactPointParameterization(generic_object)\n    boundary_length = generic_object.boundary_length\n    print(f\"  Boundary length: {boundary_length:.3f} m\")\n    \n    # Visualize parameterization using matplotlib\n    print(f\"\\nGenerating parameterization visualization...\")\n    try:\n        ax = parameterization.visualize_parameterization(n_test_points=30)\n        \n        # Save plot if save-dir is provided\n        if args.save_dir:\n            save_path = Path(args.save_dir)\n            save_path.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)\n            plot_file = save_path / f\"{args.obj_shape}_parameterization.png\"\n            plt.savefig(plot_file, dpi=150, bbox_inches='tight')\n            print(f\"  ✓ Saved parameterization plot to: {plot_file}\")\n        else:\n            # Save to current directory as fallback\n            plot_file = Path(f\"{args.obj_shape}_parameterization.png\")\n            plt.savefig(plot_file, dpi=150, bbox_inches='tight')\n            print(f\"  ✓ Saved parameterization plot to: {plot_file}\")\n        \n        plt.close()\n    except Exception as e:\n        print(f\"  ⚠ Failed to generate visualization: {e}\")\n        import traceback\n        traceback.print_exc()\n    \n    # Delay 1 second to let physics stabilize\n    print(f\"\\nWaiting 1 second for physics to stabilize...\")\n    for _ in range(int(1.0 / TIMESTEP)):\n        pyb.stepSimulation()\n        if not args.no_gui:\n            time.sleep(TIMESTEP)\n    print(f\"  ✓ Physics stabilized\")\n    \n    # Traverse through t_param and visualize\n    print(f\"\\n{'='*60}\")\n    print(f\"  Traversing t_param: increment by {T_PARAM_INCREMENT:.1f} every {T_PARAM_INCREMENT_INTERVAL:.1f} seconds...\")\n    print(f\"{'='*60}\")\n    \n    n_steps = int(args.duration / TIMESTEP)\n    step_count = 0\n    t = 0.0\n    current_t_param = 0.0\n    last_increment_time = 0.0\n    \n    # Markers (will be updated each step)\n    contact_marker = None\n    normal_outward_marker = None\n    normal_inward_marker = None\n    tangent_marker = None\n    \n    for step in range(n_steps):\n        # Only update markers when t_param changes\n        if t_param_changed:\n            # Get contact point info at current t_param.\n            # NOTE: ContactPointParameterization already works in world coordinates\n            # Remove old markers\n            if contact_marker is not None:\n                pyb.removeBody(contact_marker)\n            if normal_outward_marker is not None:\n                pyb.removeBody(normal_outward_marker)\n            if normal_inward_marker is not None:\n                pyb.removeBody(normal_inward_marker)\n            if tangent_marker is not None:\n                pyb.removeBody(tangent_marker)\n            \n            # Print status when t_param changes\n            print(f\"  [t={t:.2f}s] t_param={current_t_param:.3f}, \"\n                  f\"contact_point_world=({contact_point_world[0]:.3f}, {contact_point_world[1]:.3f})\")\n        \n        pyb.stepSimulation()\n        t += TIMESTEP\n        step_count += 1\n        \n        if not args.no_gui:\n            time.sleep(TIMESTEP * 0.5)\n    \n    print(f\"\\n{'='*60}\")\n    print(\"  VISUALIZATION COMPLETE\")\n    print(f\"{'='*60}\")\n    print(f\"  Red sphere: Contact point position (GenericObject's understanding)\")\n    print(f\"  Green arrow: Normal outward vector (from GenericObject)\")\n    print(f\"  Yellow arrow: Normal inward vector (for comparison)\")\n    print(f\"  Blue arrow: Tangent vector\")\n    print(f\"  Compare markers with actual 3D object to verify conversion correctness\")\n    print(f\"{'='*60}\")\n    \n    if not args.no_gui:\n        print(\"\\nMarkers will remain visible. Tuple[float, float, float]:\n    \"\"\"Calculate 3D inertia tensor diagonal from 2D moment of inertia.\n    \n    For a 2D shape extruded to height h, the 3D inertia tensor is:\n    - Ixx: rotation around x-axis (involves height and y-extent)\n    - Iyy: rotation around y-axis (involves height and x-extent)\n    - Izz: rotation around z-axis (the original 2D moment of inertia)\n    \n    Parameters\n    ----------\n    moment_of_inertia_2d : float\n        The 2D moment of inertia (Iz) from GenericObject.\n    mass : float\n        Object mass.\n    height : float\n        Extrusion height of the object.\n    \n    Returns\n    -------\n    tuple\n        (Ixx, Iyy, Izz) inertia tensor diagonal.\n    \"\"\"\n    # For a 2D shape extruded to height h:\n    # Izz = I_2d (the planar moment of inertia)\n    # Ixx ≈ Iyy ≈ I_2d/2 + m*h²/12 (parallel axis theorem for height)\n    Izz = moment_of_inertia_2d\n    \n    # Approximation for Ixx, Iyy (assuming roughly symmetric shape)\n    height_contribution = mass * height * height / 12.0\n    Ixx = Izz / 2.0 + height_contribution\n    Iyy = Izz / 2.0 + height_contribution\n    \n    return (Ixx, Iyy, Izz)\n\n\n# ============================================================================\n# CONVEX DECOMPOSITION UTILITIES\n# ============================================================================\n\ndef is_convex(polygon: Polygon) -&gt; pyb.getQuaternionFromEuler([0, 0, orientation])\n    pos = [position[0] + centroid_coords[0], \n           position[1] + centroid_coords[1], \n           height / 2]\n    \n    # Create multibody with explicit inertia\n    uid = pyb.createMultiBody(\n        baseMass=mass,\n        baseInertialFramePosition=[0, 0, 0],\n        baseInertialFrameOrientation=[0, 0, 0, 1],\n        baseCollisionShapeIndex=collision_id,\n        baseVisualShapeIndex=visual_id,\n        basePosition=pos,\n        baseOrientation=orn\n    )\n    \n    # Set dynamics properties including inertia and friction\n    pyb.changeDynamics(\n        uid, -1,\n        mass=mass,\n        localInertiaDiagonal=list(inertia_3d),\n        lateralFriction=object_friction,\n        spinningFriction=0.01,\n        rollingFriction=0.01,\n        linearDamping=0.0,\n        angularDamping=0.0\n    )\n    \n    return uid\n\n\ndef _create_triangle_mesh(coords_2d, height):\n    \"\"\"Create a 3D triangle mesh from 2D coordinates.\n    \n    ⚠️  KNOWN ISSUE: Triangle physics is wrong (objects don't rotate when pushed at corners).\n        This is weird since triangles should be simpler than rectilinear shapes.\n        The more complex shapes (L/T) work but the simple triangle doesn't.\n        Double-check this implementation vs rectilinear shape creation.\n        Possible issues: mesh vertex ordering, inertia calculation, or mass distribution.\n    \n    Parameters\n    ----------\n    coords_2d : list\n        List of 3 (x, y) coordinates\n    height : float\n        Extrusion height\n    \n    Returns\n    -------\n    tuple\n        (vertices_3d, indices) arrays\n    \"\"\"\n    if len(coords_2d) != 3:\n        raise ValueError(\"Triangle must have exactly 3 vertices\")\n    \n    vertices_3d = []\n    indices = []\n    \n    # Bottom face vertices (z = 0)\n    for x, y in coords_2d:\n        vertices_3d.append([x, y, 0.0])\n    \n    # Top face vertices (z = height)\n    for x, y in coords_2d:\n        vertices_3d.append([x, y, height])\n    \n    # Bottom face (counter-clockwise when viewed from below)\n    indices.append([0, 1, 2])\n    \n    # Top face (clockwise when viewed from above)\n    indices.append([3, 5, 4])\n    \n    # Side faces\n    indices.append([0, 3, 4])  # Side 0-1, triangle 1\n    indices.append([0, 4, 1])  # Side 0-1, triangle 2\n    indices.append([1, 4, 5])  # Side 1-2, triangle 1\n    indices.append([1, 5, 2])  # Side 1-2, triangle 2\n    indices.append([2, 5, 3])  # Side 2-0, triangle 1\n    indices.append([2, 3, 0])  # Side 2-0, triangle 2\n    \n    return np.array(vertices_3d, dtype=np.float64), np.array(indices, dtype=np.int32)\n\n\ndef _create_polygon_mesh(coords_2d, height):\n    \"\"\"Create a 3D polygon mesh from 2D coordinates by extrusion.\n    \n    Parameters\n    ----------\n    coords_2d : list\n        List of (x, y) coordinates\n    height : float\n        Extrusion height\n    \n    Returns\n    -------\n    tuple\n        (vertices_3d, indices) arrays\n    \"\"\"\n    n = len(coords_2d)\n    if n &lt; 3:\n        raise ValueError(\"Polygon must have at least 3 vertices\")\n    \n    vertices_3d = []\n    indices = []\n    \n    # Bottom face vertices (z = 0)\n    for x, y in coords_2d:\n        vertices_3d.append([x, y, 0.0])\n    \n    # Top face vertices (z = height)\n    for x, y in coords_2d:\n        vertices_3d.append([x, y, height])\n    \n    # Bottom face: triangulate using fan from first vertex\n    for i in range(n - 2):\n        indices.append([0, i + 1, i + 2])\n    \n    # Top face: same triangulation but reversed winding\n    top_base = n\n    for i in range(n - 2):\n        indices.append([top_base, top_base + i + 2, top_base + i + 1])\n    \n    # Side faces: connect bottom and top outlines\n    for i in range(n):\n        next_i = (i + 1) % n\n        # Create two triangles for each side face\n        indices.append([i, next_i, top_base + next_i])\n        indices.append([i, top_base + next_i, top_base + i])\n    \n    return np.array(vertices_3d, dtype=np.float64), np.array(indices, dtype=np.int32)\n\n\ndef _create_compound_body(\n    parts: List[Polygon],\n    physics_props: Dict,\n    height: float,\n    position: Tuple[float, float, float],\n    orientation: float,\n    color: Tuple[float, float, float, float]\n) -&gt; int:\n    \"\"\"Create a compound PyBullet body from multiple convex polygons.\n    \n    Parameters\n    ----------\n    parts : list of Polygon\n        List of convex polygons forming the compound shape.\n    physics_props : dict\n        Physics properties including 'mass', 'inertia_3d', 'lateral_friction'.\n    height : float\n        Extrusion height.\n    position : tuple\n        (x, y, z) world position.\n    orientation : float\n        Z-axis rotation in radians.\n    color : tuple\n        RGBA color.\n    \n    Returns\n    -------\n    int\n        PyBullet body UID.\n    \"\"\"\n    if len(parts) == 0:\n        raise ValueError(\"No parts provided for compound body\")\n    \n    total_mass = physics_props['mass']\n    inertia_3d = physics_props['inertia_3d']\n    object_friction = physics_props['object_friction']\n    \n    # Calculate mass distribution based on area\n    total_area = sum(p.area for p in parts)\n    masses = [total_mass * p.area / total_area for p in parts]\n    \n    # Create collision and visual shapes for each part\n    collision_ids = []\n    visual_ids = []\n    positions = []\n    \n    # Use first part as base\n    base_centroid = np.array(parts[0].centroid.coords[0])\n    \n    for i, (part, part_mass) in enumerate(zip(parts, masses)):\n        bounds = part.bounds\n        half_extents = [\n            (bounds[2] - bounds[0]) / 2,\n            (bounds[3] - bounds[1]) / 2,\n            height / 2\n        ]\n        \n        collision_id = pyb.createCollisionShape(\n            shapeType=pyb.GEOM_BOX,\n            halfExtents=half_extents\n        )\n        collision_ids.append(collision_id)\n        \n        visual_id = pyb.createVisualShape(\n            shapeType=pyb.GEOM_BOX,\n            halfExtents=half_extents,\n            rgbaColor=color\n        )\n        visual_ids.append(visual_id)\n        \n        # Position relative to base centroid\n        centroid = np.array(part.centroid.coords[0])\n        rel_pos = centroid - base_centroid\n        positions.append([rel_pos[0], rel_pos[1], 0])\n    \n    # Create multi-body\n    orn = pyb.getQuaternionFromEuler([0, 0, orientation])\n    pos = list(position)\n    pos[0] += base_centroid[0]\n    pos[1] += base_centroid[1]\n    pos[2] = height / 2\n    \n    if len(parts) == 1:\n        uid = pyb.createMultiBody(\n            baseMass=total_mass,\n            baseInertialFramePosition=[0, 0, 0],\n            baseInertialFrameOrientation=[0, 0, 0, 1],\n            baseCollisionShapeIndex=collision_ids[0],\n            baseVisualShapeIndex=visual_ids[0],\n            basePosition=pos,\n            baseOrientation=orn\n        )\n    else:\n        # Build link arrays\n        link_masses = masses[1:]\n        link_collision_ids = collision_ids[1:]\n        link_visual_ids = visual_ids[1:]\n        link_positions = positions[1:]\n        link_orientations = [[0, 0, 0, 1]] * len(link_masses)\n        link_inertial_positions = [[0, 0, 0]] * len(link_masses)\n        link_inertial_orientations = [[0, 0, 0, 1]] * len(link_masses)\n        link_parent_indices = [0] * len(link_masses)\n        link_joint_types = [pyb.JOINT_FIXED] * len(link_masses)\n        link_joint_axes = [[0, 0, 1]] * len(link_masses)\n        \n        uid = pyb.createMultiBody(\n            baseMass=masses[0],\n            baseInertialFramePosition=[0, 0, 0],\n            baseInertialFrameOrientation=[0, 0, 0, 1],\n            baseCollisionShapeIndex=collision_ids[0],\n            baseVisualShapeIndex=visual_ids[0],\n            basePosition=pos,\n            baseOrientation=orn,\n            linkMasses=link_masses,\n            linkCollisionShapeIndices=link_collision_ids,\n            linkVisualShapeIndices=link_visual_ids,\n            linkPositions=link_positions,\n            linkOrientations=link_orientations,\n            linkInertialFramePositions=link_inertial_positions,\n            linkInertialFrameOrientations=link_inertial_orientations,\n            linkParentIndices=link_parent_indices,\n            linkJointTypes=link_joint_types,\n            linkJointAxis=link_joint_axes\n        )\n    \n    # Set dynamics properties for base\n    pyb.changeDynamics(\n        uid, -1,\n        localInertiaDiagonal=list(inertia_3d),\n        lateralFriction=object_friction,\n        spinningFriction=0.01,\n        rollingFriction=0.01,\n        linearDamping=0.0,\n        angularDamping=0.0\n    )\n    \n    # Set friction for all links\n    for i in range(len(parts) - 1):\n        pyb.changeDynamics(\n            uid, i,\n            lateralFriction=object_friction,\n            spinningFriction=0.01,\n            rollingFriction=0.01\n        )\n    \n    return uid\n\n\n# ============================================================================\n# PYBULLET TO GENERIC CONVERSION\n# ============================================================================\n\n# TODO: Implement OBJ-based workflow here\n#   Function: obj_to_generic(obj_path: str, shape_name: str, \n#                            position: Tuple, orientation: float) -&gt; Tuple[GenericObject, int]\n#   - Load OBJ file into PyBullet using createCollisionShape/createVisualShape\n#   - Extract physics properties (mass, inertia) from PyBullet\n#   - Use hardcoded 2D vertices for the shape (from top view)\n#   - Create GenericObject with extracted properties\n#   - Return (GenericObject, pybullet_uid)\n#\n#   This is the \"backward\" workflow: PyBullet -&gt; GenericObject\n#   But ensures correct physics since OBJ files have proper collision meshes\n\ndef pybullet_to_generic(\n    uid: int,\n    link_idx: int = -1,\n    name: str = \"PyBulletObject\"\n) -&gt; GenericObject:\n    \"\"\"Convert a PyBullet body to a GenericObject.\n    \n    Extracts physics properties:\n    - mass\n    - moment_of_inertia (from Izz component)\n    - lateral_friction\n    \n    Parameters\n    ----------\n    uid : int\n        PyBullet body UID.\n    link_idx : int\n        Link index (-1 for base).\n    name : str\n        Name for the GenericObject.\n    \n    Returns\n    -------\n    GenericObject\n        Shapely-based object with physics properties.\n    \"\"\"\n    # Get collision shape data\n    shape_data = pyb.getCollisionShapeData(uid, link_idx)\n    \n    if len(shape_data) == 0:\n        raise ValueError(f\"No collision shape found for body {uid}, link {link_idx}\")\n    \n    shape_type = shape_data[0][2]\n    dimensions = shape_data[0][3]\n    \n    # Get dynamics info\n    # Returns: mass, lateral_friction, local_inertia_diagonal, local_inertial_pos, \n    #          local_inertial_orn, restitution, rolling_friction, spinning_friction,\n    #          contact_damping, contact_stiffness, body_type, collision_margin\n    dynamics = pyb.getDynamicsInfo(uid, link_idx)\n    mass = dynamics[0]\n    friction = dynamics[1]\n    local_inertia = dynamics[2]  # (Ixx, Iyy, Izz)\n    \n    # Extract Izz as 2D moment of inertia\n    moment_of_inertia = local_inertia[2] if len(local_inertia) &gt;= 3 else 0.1\n    \n    # Get current pose\n    if link_idx == -1:\n        pos, orn = pyb.getBasePositionAndOrientation(uid)\n    else:\n        link_state = pyb.getLinkState(uid, link_idx)\n        pos, orn = link_state[0], link_state[1]\n    \n    euler = pyb.getEulerFromQuaternion(orn)\n    heading = euler[2]\n    \n    # Create geometry based on shape type\n    if shape_type == pyb.GEOM_BOX:\n        half_extents = dimensions\n        vertices = [\n            (-half_extents[0], -half_extents[1]),\n            (half_extents[0], -half_extents[1]),\n            (half_extents[0], half_extents[1]),\n            (-half_extents[0], half_extents[1])\n        ]\n        geometry = Polygon(vertices)\n        \n    elif shape_type == pyb.GEOM_CYLINDER or shape_type == pyb.GEOM_SPHERE:\n        radius = dimensions[1] if shape_type == pyb.GEOM_CYLINDER else dimensions[0]\n        geometry = Point(0, 0).buffer(radius, resolution=32)\n        \n    elif shape_type == pyb.GEOM_MESH:\n        # Try to extract vertices from mesh\n        # This is limited - mesh data not easily accessible\n        # Fallback to bounding box\n        aabb_min, aabb_max = pyb.getAABB(uid, link_idx)\n        half_x = (aabb_max[0] - aabb_min[0]) / 2\n        half_y = (aabb_max[1] - aabb_min[1]) / 2\n        vertices = [\n            (-half_x, -half_y), (half_x, -half_y),\n            (half_x, half_y), (-half_x, half_y)\n        ]\n        geometry = Polygon(vertices)\n    else:\n        # Unknown shape - use AABB\n        aabb_min, aabb_max = pyb.getAABB(uid, link_idx)\n        half_x = (aabb_max[0] - aabb_min[0]) / 2\n        half_y = (aabb_max[1] - aabb_min[1]) / 2\n        vertices = [\n            (-half_x, -half_y), (half_x, -half_y),\n            (half_x, half_y), (-half_x, half_y)\n        ]\n        geometry = Polygon(vertices)\n    \n    # Create GenericObject with all extracted physics properties\n    obj = GenericObject(\n        geometry=geometry,\n        mass=mass if mass &gt; 0 else 1.0,\n        moment_of_inertia=moment_of_inertia,\n        lateral_friction=friction,\n        heading=heading,\n        name=name\n    )\n    obj.position = np.array([pos[0], pos[1]])\n    \n    return obj\n\n\ndef print_physics_comparison(generic_obj: GenericObject, pybullet_uid: int, height: float = DEFAULT_HEIGHT):\n    \"\"\"Print comparison of physics properties between GenericObject and PyBullet body.\n    \n    Useful for debugging and verifying physics property transfer.\n    \n    Friction terminology:\n    - kinetic_friction / static_friction: ground-object friction (in GenericObject)\n    - lateral_friction: object-robot contact friction (in GenericObject)\n    - PyBullet lateralFriction: general dry friction coefficient\n    \n    Parameters\n    ----------\n    generic_obj : GenericObject\n        Original Shapely-based object.\n    pybullet_uid : int\n        PyBullet body UID.\n    height : float\n        Extrusion height used.\n    \"\"\"\n    dynamics = pyb.getDynamicsInfo(pybullet_uid, -1)\n    pyb_mass = dynamics[0]\n    pyb_friction = dynamics[1]\n    pyb_inertia = dynamics[2]\n    \n    kinetic_friction = getattr(generic_obj, 'kinetic_friction', 0.2)\n    inertia_3d = calculate_3d_inertia_from_2d(generic_obj.moment_of_inertia, generic_obj.mass, height)\n    \n    print(\"\\n\" + \"=\"*60)\n    print(f\"  PHYSICS PROPERTIES COMPARISON: {generic_obj.name}\")\n    print(\"=\"*60)\n    print(f\"  {'Property':&lt;25} {'GenericObject':&lt;15} {'PyBullet':&lt;15}\")\n    print(\"-\"*60)\n    print(f\"  {'Mass (kg)':&lt;25} {generic_obj.mass:&lt;15.4f} {pyb_mass:&lt;15.4f}\")\n    print(f\"  {'Contact Friction':&lt;25} {generic_obj.lateral_friction:&lt;15.4f} {pyb_friction:&lt;15.4f}\")\n    print(f\"  {'Ground Friction (μk)':&lt;25} {kinetic_friction:&lt;15.4f} {'(via ground)':&lt;15}\")\n    print(f\"  {'Moment of Inertia (2D)':&lt;25} {generic_obj.moment_of_inertia:&lt;15.4f} {pyb_inertia[2]:&lt;15.4f}\")\n    print(\"-\"*60)\n    print(f\"  {'Inertia Ixx':&lt;25} {inertia_3d[0]:&lt;15.4f} {pyb_inertia[0]:&lt;15.4f}\")\n    print(f\"  {'Inertia Iyy':&lt;25} {inertia_3d[1]:&lt;15.4f} {pyb_inertia[1]:&lt;15.4f}\")\n    print(f\"  {'Inertia Izz':&lt;25} {inertia_3d[2]:&lt;15.4f} {pyb_inertia[2]:&lt;15.4f}\")\n    print(\"=\"*60)\n\n\ndef obj_to_generic(\n    obj_path: str,\n    shape_name: str,\n    position: Tuple[float, float, float] = (0, 0, 0),\n    orientation: float = 0.0,\n    mass: float = 1.0,\n    lateral_friction: float = 0.8,\n    **kwargs\n) -&gt; Tuple[GenericObject, int]:\n    \"\"\"Load object from OBJ file and create GenericObject from it.\n    \n    This is the \"backward\" workflow: PyBullet -&gt; GenericObject\n    Used for shapes with physics issues (triangle, L-shape, T-shape).\n    \n    Workflow:\n    1. Load OBJ file into PyBullet using createCollisionShape/createVisualShape\n    2. Set physics properties (mass, inertia) manually or extract from PyBullet\n    3. Load 2D vertices from the corresponding DXF file via dxf_to_generic\n    4. Create GenericObject with extracted properties\n    \n    Parameters\n    ----------\n    obj_path : str\n        Path to OBJ file (relative to package urdf directory or absolute)\n    shape_name : str\n        Name of the shape (used to locate the corresponding DXF file: &#96;&#96;&lt;shape_name&gt;.dxf&#96;&#96;)\n    position : tuple\n        (x, y, z) position in world frame\n    orientation : float\n        Rotation around z-axis in radians\n    mass : float\n        Mass of the object (default: 1.0 kg)\n    lateral_friction : float\n        Lateral friction coefficient (default: 0.8)\n    **kwargs\n        Additional arguments (e.g., moment_of_inertia) for physics properties\n    \n    Returns\n    -------\n    tuple\n        (GenericObject, pybullet_uid)\n    \"\"\"\n    # Resolve OBJ path\n    if not Path(obj_path).is_absolute():\n        # Try package urdf directory first\n        obj_full_path = Path(pkg_path) / \"urdf\" / obj_path\n        if not obj_full_path.exists():\n            # Fallback to provided path\n            obj_full_path = Path(obj_path)\n        obj_path = str(obj_full_path)\n    \n    if not Path(obj_path).exists():\n        raise FileNotFoundError(f\"OBJ file not found: {obj_path}\")\n    \n    # Convert orientation to quaternion\n    orientation_quat = pyb.getQuaternionFromEuler([0, 0, orientation])\n    \n    # Choose a simple per-shape color (MTL files are not reliably used by PyBullet\n    # when loading raw OBJ meshes, so we assign colors explicitly here).\n    shape_colors = {\n        'right_triangle': (0.8, 0.3, 0.3, 1.0),\n        'scalene_triangle': (0.3, 0.8, 0.3, 1.0),\n        'equilateral_triangle': (0.3, 0.3, 0.8, 1.0),\n        'l_shape': (0.8, 0.6, 0.2, 1.0),\n        'asym_l_shape': (0.6, 0.2, 0.8, 1.0),\n        't_shape': (0.2, 0.8, 0.8, 1.0),\n        'asym_t_shape': (0.8, 0.2, 0.5, 1.0),\n        'hourglass': (0.7, 0.7, 0.2, 1.0),\n        'bolt': (0.8, 0.8, 0.8, 1.0),\n        'pi': (0.9, 0.7, 0.3, 1.0),\n        'root': (0.6, 0.9, 0.6, 1.0),\n    }\n    rgba = shape_colors.get(shape_name, (0.8, 0.8, 0.8, 1.0))\n\n    # Load OBJ file into PyBullet (similar to test_display_obj.py)\n    collision_shape_id = pyb.createCollisionShape(\n        shapeType=pyb.GEOM_MESH,\n        fileName=obj_path,\n        flags=pyb.URDF_INITIALIZE_SAT_FEATURES\n    )\n    \n    visual_shape_id = pyb.createVisualShape(\n        shapeType=pyb.GEOM_MESH,\n        fileName=obj_path,\n        rgbaColor=rgba,\n    )\n    \n    # Create multi-body\n    body_uid = pyb.createMultiBody(\n        baseMass=mass,\n        baseCollisionShapeIndex=collision_shape_id,\n        baseVisualShapeIndex=visual_shape_id,\n        basePosition=position,\n        baseOrientation=orientation_quat\n    )\n    \n    # Set dynamics properties\n    pyb.changeDynamics(\n        body_uid, -1,\n        lateralFriction=lateral_friction\n    )\n    \n    # Extract physics properties from PyBullet (after setting them)\n    dynamics_info = pyb.getDynamicsInfo(body_uid, -1)\n    actual_mass = dynamics_info[0]\n    actual_lateral_friction = dynamics_info[1]\n    local_inertia_diagonal = dynamics_info[2]  # (Ixx, Iyy, Izz)\n    moment_of_inertia = kwargs.get('moment_of_inertia', local_inertia_diagonal[2])  # Izz for 2D\n\n    # Create GenericObject geometry from DXF (new pipeline)\n    dxf_path = Path(pkg_path) / \"urdf\" / f\"{shape_name}.dxf\"\n    if not dxf_path.exists():\n        raise FileNotFoundError(f\"DXF file for shape '{shape_name}' not found: {dxf_path}\")\n\n    generic_obj = dxf_to_generic(\n        dxf_path=dxf_path,\n        name=shape_name,\n        mass=actual_mass if actual_mass &gt; 0 else mass,\n        lateral_friction=actual_lateral_friction,\n        heading=orientation,\n    )\n    generic_obj.position = np.array([position[0], position[1]])\n\n    # Override moment_of_inertia if we have a better estimate from PyBullet\n    generic_obj.moment_of_inertia = moment_of_inertia\n\n    return generic_obj, body_uid\n\n\n# ============================================================================\n# STANDARD OBJECTS FACTORY\n# ============================================================================\n\ndef create_standard_pybullet_objects(\n    height: float = DEFAULT_HEIGHT,\n    spacing: float = 1.0\n) -&gt; Dict[str, Tuple[GenericObject, int]]:\n    \"\"\"Create all standard shapes in PyBullet.\n    \n    Parameters\n    ----------\n    height : float\n        Extrusion height for all shapes.\n    spacing : float\n        Spacing between objects in the scene.\n    \n    Returns\n    -------\n    dict\n        Mapping from shape name to (GenericObject, pybullet_uid) tuple.\n    \"\"\"\n    standard_objects = create_standard_objects()\n    result = {}\n    \n    # Colors for different shapes\n    colors = {\n        'rectangle': (0.8, 0.4, 0.2, 1.0),\n        'circle': (0.2, 0.6, 0.8, 1.0),\n        'ellipse': (0.6, 0.2, 0.8, 1.0),\n        'triangle': (0.2, 0.8, 0.4, 1.0),\n        'fat_triangle': (0.8, 0.8, 0.2, 1.0),\n        'scalene': (0.8, 0.2, 0.6, 1.0),\n        'l_shape': (0.4, 0.8, 0.8, 1.0),\n        'asym_l_shape': (0.8, 0.6, 0.4, 1.0),\n        't_shape': (0.2, 0.8, 0.2, 1.0),\n        'plus_shape': (0.6, 0.6, 0.8, 1.0),\n    }\n    \n    # Grid layout\n    n_cols = 4\n    col = 0\n    row = 0\n    \n    for name, generic_obj in standard_objects.items():\n        x = col * spacing\n        y = row * spacing\n        position = (x, y, 0)\n        \n        color = colors.get(name, DEFAULT_COLOR)\n        \n        try:\n            uid = generic_to_pybullet(\n                generic_obj, height=height, position=position, color=color\n            )\n            result[name] = (generic_obj, uid)\n            print(f\"  Created {name} at ({x:.1f}, {y:.1f})\")\n        except Exception as e:\n            print(f\"  Failed to create {name}: {e}\")\n        \n        col += 1\n        if col &gt;= n_cols:\n            col = 0\n            row += 1\n    \n    return result\n\n\n# ============================================================================\n# WRAPPER CLASS FOR BRIDGED OBJECTS\n# ============================================================================\n\nclass BridgedObject:\n    \"\"\"Wrapper that maintains both GenericObject and PyBullet representations.\n    \n    Keeps the two representations synchronized.\n    \"\"\"\n    \n    def __init__(self, generic_obj: GenericObject, pybullet_uid: int):\n        \"\"\"Initialize with both representations.\n        \n len(set(xs)) == 2\n        y_unique = len(set(ys)) == 2\n        \n        if x_unique and y_unique:\n            # Use box for rectangles/squares\n            collision_id = pyb.createCollisionShape(\n                shapeType=pyb.GEOM_BOX,\n                halfExtents=half_extents\n            )\n            visual_id = pyb.createVisualShape(\n                shapeType=pyb.GEOM_BOX,\n                halfExtents=half_extents,\n                rgbaColor=color\n            )\n        else:\n            # Non-axis-aligned quadrilateral, use mesh\n            vertices_3d, indices = _create_polygon_mesh(coords, height)\n            collision_id = pyb.createCollisionShape(\n                shapeType=pyb.GEOM_MESH,\n                vertices=vertices_3d.tolist(),\n                indices=indices.flatten().tolist()\n            )\n            visual_id = pyb.createVisualShape(\n                shapeType=pyb.GEOM_MESH,\n                vertices=vertices_3d.tolist(),\n                indices=indices.flatten().tolist(),\n                rgbaColor=color\n            )\n    else:\n        # For other polygons, use mesh\n        vertices_3d, indices = _create_polygon_mesh(coords, height)\n        collision_id = pyb.createCollisionShape(\n            shapeType=pyb.GEOM_MESH,\n            vertices=vertices_3d.tolist(),\n            indices=indices.flatten().tolist()\n        )\n        visual_id = pyb.createVisualShape(\n            shapeType=pyb.GEOM_MESH,\n            vertices=vertices_3d.tolist(),\n            indices=indices.flatten().tolist(),\n            rgbaColor=color\n        )\n    \n    # Create body at centroid\n    centroid_coords = list(centroid.coords)[0]\n    orn = pyb.getQuaternionFromEuler([0, 0, orientation])\n    pos = [position[0] + centroid_coords[0], \n           position[1] + centroid_coords[1], \n           height / 2]\n    \n    # Create multibody with explicit inertia\n    uid = pyb.createMultiBody(\n        baseMass=mass,\n        baseInertialFramePosition=[0, 0, 0],\n        baseInertialFrameOrientation=[0, 0, 0, 1],\n        baseCollisionShapeIndex=collision_id,\n        baseVisualShapeIndex=visual_id,\n        basePosition=pos,\n        baseOrientation=orn\n    )\n    \n    # Set dynamics properties including inertia and friction\n    pyb.changeDynamics(\n        uid, -1,\n        mass=mass,\n        localInertiaDiagonal=list(inertia_3d),\n        lateralFriction=object_friction,\n        spinningFriction=0.01,\n        rollingFriction=0.01,\n        linearDamping=0.0,\n        angularDamping=0.0\n    )\n    \n    return uid\n\n\ndef _create_triangle_mesh(coords_2d, height):\n    \"\"\"Create a 3D triangle mesh from 2D coordinates.\n    \n    ⚠️  KNOWN ISSUE: Triangle physics is wrong (objects don't rotate when pushed at corners).\n        This is weird since triangles should be simpler than rectilinear shapes.\n        The more complex shapes (L/T) work but the simple triangle doesn't.\n        Double-check this implementation vs rectilinear shape creation.\n        Possible issues: mesh vertex ordering, inertia calculation, or mass distribution.\n    \n    Parameters\n    ----------\n    coords_2d : list\n        List of 3 (x, y) coordinates\n    height : float\n        Extrusion height\n    \n    Returns\n    -------\n    tuple\n        (vertices_3d, indices) arrays\n    \"\"\"\n    if len(coords_2d) != 3:\n        raise ValueError(\"Triangle must have exactly 3 vertices\")\n    \n    vertices_3d = []\n    indices = []\n    \n    # Bottom face vertices (z = 0)\n    for x, y in coords_2d:\n        vertices_3d.append([x, y, 0.0])\n    \n    # Top face vertices (z = height)\n    for x, y in coords_2d:\n        vertices_3d.append([x, y, height])\n    \n    # Bottom face (counter-clockwise when viewed from below)\n    indices.append([0, 1, 2])\n    \n    # Top face (clockwise when viewed from above)\n    indices.append([3, 5, 4])\n    \n    # Side faces\n    indices.append([0, 3, 4])  # Side 0-1, triangle 1\n    indices.append([0, 4, 1])  # Side 0-1, triangle 2\n    indices.append([1, 4, 5])  # Side 1-2, triangle 1\n    indices.append([1, 5, 2])  # Side 1-2, triangle 2\n    indices.append([2, 5, 3])  # Side 2-0, triangle 1\n    indices.append([2, 3, 0])  # Side 2-0, triangle 2\n    \n    return np.array(vertices_3d, dtype=np.float64), np.array(indices, dtype=np.int32)\n\n\ndef _create_polygon_mesh(coords_2d, height):\n    \"\"\"Create a 3D polygon mesh from 2D coordinates by extrusion.\n    \n    Parameters\n    ----------\n    coords_2d : list\n        List of (x, y) coordinates\n    height : float\n        Extrusion height\n    \n    Returns\n    -------\n    tuple\n        (vertices_3d, indices) arrays\n    \"\"\"\n    n = len(coords_2d)\n    if n &lt; 3:\n        raise ValueError(\"Polygon must have at least 3 vertices\")\n    \n    vertices_3d = []\n    indices = []\n    \n    # Bottom face vertices (z = 0)\n    for x, y in coords_2d:\n        vertices_3d.append([x, y, 0.0])\n    \n    # Top face vertices (z = height)\n    for x, y in coords_2d:\n        vertices_3d.append([x, y, height])\n    \n    # Bottom face: triangulate using fan from first vertex\n    for i in range(n - 2):\n        indices.append([0, i + 1, i + 2])\n    \n    # Top face: same triangulation but reversed winding\n    top_base = n\n    for i in range(n - 2):\n        indices.append([top_base, top_base + i + 2, top_base + i + 1])\n    \n    # Side faces: connect bottom and top outlines\n    for i in range(n):\n        next_i = (i + 1) % n\n        # Create two triangles for each side face\n        indices.append([i, next_i, top_base + next_i])\n        indices.append([i, top_base + next_i, top_base + i])\n    \n    return np.array(vertices_3d, dtype=np.float64), np.array(indices, dtype=np.int32)\n\n\ndef _create_compound_body(\n    parts: List[Polygon],\n    physics_props: Dict,\n    height: float,\n    position: Tuple[float, float, float],\n    orientation: float,\n    color: Tuple[float, float, float, float]\n) -&gt; int:\n    \"\"\"Create a compound PyBullet body from multiple convex polygons.\n    \n    Parameters\n    ----------\n    parts : list of Polygon\n        List of convex polygons forming the compound shape.\n    physics_props : dict\n        Physics properties including 'mass', 'inertia_3d', 'lateral_friction'.\n    height : float\n        Extrusion height.\n    position : tuple\n        (x, y, z) world position.\n    orientation : float\n        Z-axis rotation in radians.\n    color : tuple\n        RGBA color.\n    \n    Returns\n    -------\n    int\n        PyBullet body UID.\n    \"\"\"\n    if len(parts) == 0:\n        raise ValueError(\"No parts provided for compound body\")\n    \n    total_mass = physics_props['mass']\n    inertia_3d = physics_props['inertia_3d']\n    object_friction = physics_props['object_friction']\n    \n    # Calculate mass distribution based on area\n    total_area = sum(p.area for p in parts)\n    masses = [total_mass * p.area / total_area for p in parts]\n    \n    # Create collision and visual shapes for each part\n    collision_ids = []\n    visual_ids = []\n    positions = []\n    \n    # Use first part as base\n    base_centroid = np.array(parts[0].centroid.coords[0])\n    \n    for i, (part, part_mass) in enumerate(zip(parts, masses)):\n        bounds = part.bounds\n        half_extents = [\n            (bounds[2] - bounds[0]) / 2,\n            (bounds[3] - bounds[1]) / 2,\n            height / 2\n        ]\n        \n        collision_id = pyb.createCollisionShape(\n            shapeType=pyb.GEOM_BOX,\n            halfExtents=half_extents\n        )\n        collision_ids.append(collision_id)\n        \n        visual_id = pyb.createVisualShape(\n            shapeType=pyb.GEOM_BOX,\n            halfExtents=half_extents,\n            rgbaColor=color\n        )\n        visual_ids.append(visual_id)\n        \n        # Position relative to base centroid\n        centroid = np.array(part.centroid.coords[0])\n        rel_pos = centroid - base_centroid\n        positions.append([rel_pos[0], rel_pos[1], 0])\n    \n    # Create multi-body\n    orn = pyb.getQuaternionFromEuler([0, 0, orientation])\n    pos = list(position)\n    pos[0] += base_centroid[0]\n    pos[1] += base_centroid[1]\n    pos[2] = height / 2\n    \n    if len(parts) == 1:\n        uid = pyb.createMultiBody(\n            baseMass=total_mass,\n            baseInertialFramePosition=[0, 0, 0],\n            baseInertialFrameOrientation=[0, 0, 0, 1],\n            baseCollisionShapeIndex=collision_ids[0],\n            baseVisualShapeIndex=visual_ids[0],\n            basePosition=pos,\n            baseOrientation=orn\n        )\n    else:\n        # Build link arrays\n        link_masses = masses[1:]\n        link_collision_ids = collision_ids[1:]\n        link_visual_ids = visual_ids[1:]\n        link_positions = positions[1:]\n        link_orientations = [[0, 0, 0, 1]] * len(link_masses)\n        link_inertial_positions = [[0, 0, 0]] * len(link_masses)\n        link_inertial_orientations = [[0, 0, 0, 1]] * len(link_masses)\n        link_parent_indices = [0] * len(link_masses)\n        link_joint_types = [pyb.JOINT_FIXED] * len(link_masses)\n        link_joint_axes = [[0, 0, 1]] * len(link_masses)\n        \n        uid = pyb.createMultiBody(\n            baseMass=masses[0],\n            baseInertialFramePosition=[0, 0, 0],\n            baseInertialFrameOrientation=[0, 0, 0, 1],\n            baseCollisionShapeIndex=collision_ids[0],\n            baseVisualShapeIndex=visual_ids[0],\n            basePosition=pos,\n            baseOrientation=orn,\n            linkMasses=link_masses,\n            linkCollisionShapeIndices=link_collision_ids,\n            linkVisualShapeIndices=link_visual_ids,\n            linkPositions=link_positions,\n            linkOrientations=link_orientations,\n            linkInertialFramePositions=link_inertial_positions,\n            linkInertialFrameOrientations=link_inertial_orientations,\n            linkParentIndices=link_parent_indices,\n            linkJointTypes=link_joint_types,\n            linkJointAxis=link_joint_axes\n        )\n    \n    # Set dynamics properties for base\n    pyb.changeDynamics(\n        uid, -1,\n        localInertiaDiagonal=list(inertia_3d),\n        lateralFriction=object_friction,\n        spinningFriction=0.01,\n        rollingFriction=0.01,\n        linearDamping=0.0,\n        angularDamping=0.0\n    )\n    \n    # Set friction for all links\n    for i in range(len(parts) - 1):\n        pyb.changeDynamics(\n            uid, i,\n            lateralFriction=object_friction,\n            spinningFriction=0.01,\n            rollingFriction=0.01\n        )\n    \n    return uid\n\n\n# ============================================================================\n# PYBULLET TO GENERIC CONVERSION\n# ============================================================================\n\n# TODO: Implement OBJ-based workflow here\n#   Function: obj_to_generic(obj_path: str, shape_name: str, \n#                            position: Tuple, orientation: float) -&gt; Tuple[GenericObject, int]\n#   - Load OBJ file into PyBullet using createCollisionShape/createVisualShape\n#   - Extract physics properties (mass, inertia) from PyBullet\n#   - Use hardcoded 2D vertices for the shape (from top view)\n#   - Create GenericObject with extracted properties\n#   - Return (GenericObject, pybullet_uid)\n#\n#   This is the \"backward\" workflow: PyBullet -&gt; GenericObject\n#   But ensures correct physics since OBJ files have proper collision meshes\n\ndef pybullet_to_generic(\n    uid: int,\n    link_idx: int = -1,\n    name: str = \"PyBulletObject\"\n) -&gt; GenericObject:\n    \"\"\"Convert a PyBullet body to a GenericObject.\n    \n    Extracts physics properties:\n    - mass\n    - moment_of_inertia (from Izz component)\n    - lateral_friction\n    \n    Parameters\n    ----------\n    uid : int\n        PyBullet body UID.\n    link_idx : int\n        Link index (-1 for base).\n    name : str\n        Name for the GenericObject.\n    \n    Returns\n    -------\n    GenericObject\n        Shapely-based object with physics properties.\n    \"\"\"\n    # Get collision shape data\n    shape_data = pyb.getCollisionShapeData(uid, link_idx)\n    \n    if len(shape_data) == 0:\n        raise ValueError(f\"No collision shape found for body {uid}, link {link_idx}\")\n    \n    shape_type = shape_data[0][2]\n    dimensions = shape_data[0][3]\n    \n    # Get dynamics info\n    # Returns: mass, lateral_friction, local_inertia_diagonal, local_inertial_pos, \n    #          local_inertial_orn, restitution, rolling_friction, spinning_friction,\n    #          contact_damping, contact_stiffness, body_type, collision_margin\n    dynamics = pyb.getDynamicsInfo(uid, link_idx)\n    mass = dynamics[0]\n    friction = dynamics[1]\n    local_inertia = dynamics[2]  # (Ixx, Iyy, Izz)\n    \n    # Extract Izz as 2D moment of inertia\n    moment_of_inertia = local_inertia[2] if len(local_inertia) &gt;= 3 else 0.1\n    \n    # Get current pose\n    if link_idx == -1:\n        pos, orn = pyb.getBasePositionAndOrientation(uid)\n    else:\n        link_state = pyb.getLinkState(uid, link_idx)\n        pos, orn = link_state[0], link_state[1]\n    \n    euler = pyb.getEulerFromQuaternion(orn)\n    heading = euler[2]\n    \n    # Create geometry based on shape type\n    if shape_type == pyb.GEOM_BOX:\n        half_extents = dimensions\n        vertices = [\n            (-half_extents[0], -half_extents[1]),\n            (half_extents[0], -half_extents[1]),\n            (half_extents[0], half_extents[1]),\n            (-half_extents[0], half_extents[1])\n        ]\n        geometry = Polygon(vertices)\n        \n    elif shape_type == pyb.GEOM_CYLINDER or shape_type == pyb.GEOM_SPHERE:\n        radius = dimensions[1] if shape_type == pyb.GEOM_CYLINDER else dimensions[0]\n        geometry = Point(0, 0).buffer(radius, resolution=32)\n        \n    elif shape_type == pyb.GEOM_MESH:\n        # Try to extract vertices from mesh\n        # This is limited - mesh data not easily accessible\n        # Fallback to bounding box\n        aabb_min, aabb_max = pyb.getAABB(uid, link_idx)\n        half_x = (aabb_max[0] - aabb_min[0]) / 2\n        half_y = (aabb_max[1] - aabb_min[1]) / 2\n        vertices = [\n            (-half_x, -half_y), (half_x, -half_y),\n            (half_x, half_y), (-half_x, half_y)\n        ]\n        geometry = Polygon(vertices)\n    else:\n        # Unknown shape - use AABB\n        aabb_min, aabb_max = pyb.getAABB(uid, link_idx)\n        half_x = (aabb_max[0] - aabb_min[0]) / 2\n        half_y = (aabb_max[1] - aabb_min[1]) / 2\n        vertices = [\n            (-half_x, -half_y), (half_x, -half_y),\n            (half_x, half_y), (-half_x, half_y)\n        ]\n        geometry = Polygon(vertices)\n    \n    # Create GenericObject with all extracted physics properties\n    obj = GenericObject(\n        geometry=geometry,\n        mass=mass if mass &gt; 0 else 1.0,\n        moment_of_inertia=moment_of_inertia,\n        lateral_friction=friction,\n        heading=heading,\n        name=name\n    )\n    obj.position = np.array([pos[0], pos[1]])\n    \n    return obj\n\n\ndef print_physics_comparison(generic_obj: GenericObject, pybullet_uid: int, height: float = DEFAULT_HEIGHT):\n    \"\"\"Print comparison of physics properties between GenericObject and PyBullet body.\n    \n    Useful for debugging and verifying physics property transfer.\n    \n    Friction terminology:\n    - kinetic_friction / static_friction: ground-object friction (in GenericObject)\n    - lateral_friction: object-robot contact friction (in GenericObject)\n    - PyBullet lateralFriction: general dry friction coefficient\n    \n    Parameters\n    ----------\n    generic_obj : GenericObject\n        Original Shapely-based object.\n    pybullet_uid : int\n        PyBullet body UID.\n    height : float\n        Extrusion height used.\n    \"\"\"\n    dynamics = pyb.getDynamicsInfo(pybullet_uid, -1)\n    pyb_mass = dynamics[0]\n    pyb_friction = dynamics[1]\n    pyb_inertia = dynamics[2]\n    \n    kinetic_friction = getattr(generic_obj, 'kinetic_friction', 0.2)\n    inertia_3d = calculate_3d_inertia_from_2d(generic_obj.moment_of_inertia, generic_obj.mass, height)\n    \n    print(\"\\n\" + \"=\"*60)\n    print(f\"  PHYSICS PROPERTIES COMPARISON: {generic_obj.name}\")\n    print(\"=\"*60)\n    print(f\"  {'Property':&lt;25} {'GenericObject':&lt;15} {'PyBullet':&lt;15}\")\n    print(\"-\"*60)\n    print(f\"  {'Mass (kg)':&lt;25} {generic_obj.mass:&lt;15.4f} {pyb_mass:&lt;15.4f}\")\n    print(f\"  {'Contact Friction':&lt;25} {generic_obj.lateral_friction:&lt;15.4f} {pyb_friction:&lt;15.4f}\")\n    print(f\"  {'Ground Friction (μk)':&lt;25} {kinetic_friction:&lt;15.4f} {'(via ground)':&lt;15}\")\n    print(f\"  {'Moment of Inertia (2D)':&lt;25} {generic_obj.moment_of_inertia:&lt;15.4f} {pyb_inertia[2]:&lt;15.4f}\")\n    print(\"-\"*60)\n    print(f\"  {'Inertia Ixx':&lt;25} {inertia_3d[0]:&lt;15.4f} {pyb_inertia[0]:&lt;15.4f}\")\n    print(f\"  {'Inertia Iyy':&lt;25} {inertia_3d[1]:&lt;15.4f} {pyb_inertia[1]:&lt;15.4f}\")\n    print(f\"  {'Inertia Izz':&lt;25} {inertia_3d[2]:&lt;15.4f} {pyb_inertia[2]:&lt;15.4f}\")\n    print(\"=\"*60)\n\n\ndef obj_to_generic(\n    obj_path: str,\n    shape_name: str,\n    position: Tuple[float, float, float] = (0, 0, 0),\n    orientation: float = 0.0,\n    mass: float = 1.0,\n    lateral_friction: float = 0.8,\n    **kwargs\n) -&gt; Tuple[GenericObject, int]:\n    \"\"\"Load object from OBJ file and create GenericObject from it.\n    \n    This is the \"backward\" workflow: PyBullet -&gt; GenericObject\n    Used for shapes with physics issues (triangle, L-shape, T-shape).\n    \n    Workflow:\n    1. Load OBJ file into PyBullet using createCollisionShape/createVisualShape\n    2. Set physics properties (mass, inertia) manually or extract from PyBullet\n    3. Load 2D vertices from the corresponding DXF file via dxf_to_generic\n    4. Create GenericObject with extracted properties\n    \n    Parameters\n    ----------\n    obj_path : str\n        Path to OBJ file (relative to package urdf directory or absolute)\n    shape_name : str\n        Name of the shape (used to locate the corresponding DXF file: &#96;&#96;&lt;shape_name&gt;.dxf&#96;&#96;)\n    position : tuple\n        (x, y, z) position in world frame\n    orientation : float\n        Rotation around z-axis in radians\n    mass : float\n        Mass of the object (default: 1.0 kg)\n    lateral_friction : float\n        Lateral friction coefficient (default: 0.8)\n    **kwargs\n        Additional arguments (e.g., moment_of_inertia) for physics properties\n    \n    Returns\n    -------\n    tuple\n        (GenericObject, pybullet_uid)\n    \"\"\"\n    # Resolve OBJ path\n    if not Path(obj_path).is_absolute():\n        # Try package urdf directory first\n        obj_full_path = Path(pkg_path) / \"urdf\" / obj_path\n        if not obj_full_path.exists():\n            # Fallback to provided path\n            obj_full_path = Path(obj_path)\n        obj_path = str(obj_full_path)\n    \n    if not Path(obj_path).exists():\n        raise FileNotFoundError(f\"OBJ file not found: {obj_path}\")\n    \n    # Convert orientation to quaternion\n    orientation_quat = pyb.getQuaternionFromEuler([0, 0, orientation])\n    \n    # Choose a simple per-shape color (MTL files are not reliably used by PyBullet\n    # when loading raw OBJ meshes, so we assign colors explicitly here).\n    shape_colors = {\n        'right_triangle': (0.8, 0.3, 0.3, 1.0),\n        'scalene_triangle': (0.3, 0.8, 0.3, 1.0),\n        'equilateral_triangle': (0.3, 0.3, 0.8, 1.0),\n        'l_shape': (0.8, 0.6, 0.2, 1.0),\n        'asym_l_shape': (0.6, 0.2, 0.8, 1.0),\n        't_shape': (0.2, 0.8, 0.8, 1.0),\n        'asym_t_shape': (0.8, 0.2, 0.5, 1.0),\n        'hourglass': (0.7, 0.7, 0.2, 1.0),\n        'bolt': (0.8, 0.8, 0.8, 1.0),\n        'pi': (0.9, 0.7, 0.3, 1.0),\n        'root': (0.6, 0.9, 0.6, 1.0),\n    }\n    rgba = shape_colors.get(shape_name, (0.8, 0.8, 0.8, 1.0))\n\n    # Load OBJ file into PyBullet (similar to test_display_obj.py)\n    collision_shape_id = pyb.createCollisionShape(\n        shapeType=pyb.GEOM_MESH,\n        fileName=obj_path,\n        flags=pyb.URDF_INITIALIZE_SAT_FEATURES\n    )\n    \n    visual_shape_id = pyb.createVisualShape(\n        shapeType=pyb.GEOM_MESH,\n        fileName=obj_path,\n        rgbaColor=rgba,\n    )\n    \n    # Create multi-body\n    body_uid = pyb.createMultiBody(\n        baseMass=mass,\n        baseCollisionShapeIndex=collision_shape_id,\n        baseVisualShapeIndex=visual_shape_id,\n        basePosition=position,\n        baseOrientation=orientation_quat\n    )\n    \n    # Set dynamics properties\n    pyb.changeDynamics(\n        body_uid, -1,\n        lateralFriction=lateral_friction\n    )\n    \n    # Extract physics properties from PyBullet (after setting them)\n    dynamics_info = pyb.getDynamicsInfo(body_uid, -1)\n    actual_mass = dynamics_info[0]\n    actual_lateral_friction = dynamics_info[1]\n    local_inertia_diagonal = dynamics_info[2]  # (Ixx, Iyy, Izz)\n    moment_of_inertia = kwargs.get('moment_of_inertia', local_inertia_diagonal[2])  # Izz for 2D\n\n    # Create GenericObject geometry from DXF (new pipeline)\n    dxf_path = Path(pkg_path) / \"urdf\" / f\"{shape_name}.dxf\"\n    if not dxf_path.exists():\n        raise FileNotFoundError(f\"DXF file for shape '{shape_name}' not found: {dxf_path}\")\n\n    generic_obj = dxf_to_generic(\n        dxf_path=dxf_path,\n        name=shape_name,\n        mass=actual_mass if actual_mass &gt; 0 else mass,\n        lateral_friction=actual_lateral_friction,\n        heading=orientation,\n    )\n    generic_obj.position = np.array([position[0], position[1]])\n\n    # Override moment_of_inertia if we have a better estimate from PyBullet\n    generic_obj.moment_of_inertia = moment_of_inertia\n\n    return generic_obj, body_uid\n\n\n# ============================================================================\n# STANDARD OBJECTS FACTORY\n# ============================================================================\n\ndef create_standard_pybullet_objects(\n    height: float = DEFAULT_HEIGHT,\n    spacing: float = 1.0\n) -&gt; Dict[str, Tuple[GenericObject, int]]:\n    \"\"\"Create all standard shapes in PyBullet.\n    \n    Parameters\n    ----------\n    height : float\n        Extrusion height for all shapes.\n    spacing : float\n        Spacing between objects in the scene.\n    \n    Returns\n    -------\n    dict\n        Mapping from shape name to (GenericObject, pybullet_uid) tuple.\n
